The exact supplied facts (reference_inspection_facts diagnostics, inspection_equivalent_facts.states for FinishState, and fcstm_model.text absence of any outgoing FinishState edge) show FinishState is reachable from initial and has zero outgoing transitions, with no path back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode operating behavior. That is precisely satisfaction of the stable-termination obligation, not a violation of it: the candidate's own strongest_rebuttal text concedes this is 'the satisfied case.' Per the property-preserving adjudication protocol, a zero-outgoing-transition leaf is deadlock/progress evidence for a separate deadlock-freedom obligation, not evidence against this termination contract being met. Because the defeater_evidence_reference_catalog supplied for this obligation is empty, no catalog token exists to support marking any alternative reading as a surviving rebuttal or undercut; the only supportable outcome is that the exact facts satisfy the expected property, so the candidate's implied violation reading is defeated by those same exact facts rather than left as an unresolved or surviving alternative.

This is exactly the stable-termination property the NL clause demands (an end state that 'does not re-enter or cycle back into continued operating behavior'), not a deadlock/progress defect against this termination contract. The W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostic is evidence for a distinct deadlock-freedom property on operating states, not for this termination contract, and no cataloged evidence token exists to support treating it as a surviving alternative reading here.

(4) Termination contracts NL6/NL10: FinishState has no outgoing transition and is not re-entered, so termination is stable (satisfied) — omitted. (3) HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic-shift transitions (NL11) exist and are reachable per inspection facts (transition:line:63/64 with guard R45RouteToken==19/20, resolved via internal effect chaining from enter_hwy/cruise/lane_change/exit_hwy -> [*] with effect R45RouteToken=19, then HighwayMode -> UrbanMode when R45RouteToken==19); both endpoints are reachable states so NL11 endpoints are satisfied and omitted here. (4) Termination contracts NL6/NL10: FinishState has no outgoing transition and is not re-entered, so termination is stable (satisfied) — omitted. The primary derived defect is root-unreachability of the entire CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope, which independently blocks both the owner-level initial_entry (already covered by NL12-INITENTRY-1) and the two guard/trigger obligations from ever executing, and is best captured by one derived reachability contract on the owner composite, plus one derived event_consumer_coverage contract aggregating both blocked events under that same root-unreachable owner.

decisions.basis: canonical_source_ir/plantuml_source line 14; fcstm_model event declaration event:_lane_change_complete:line:6; NL requirement on lane_change_complete transition semantics.
decisions.reason: PlantUML line 14 declares 'lane_change --> cruise : [lane_change_complete]' with only a bracketed guard and no trigger keyword. Under UML 2.5.1 §14.2.3.8.3 a triggerless transition on a non-composite state (lane_change is a simple state) is a completion transition that never fires because the simple state has no internal completion event. The closed model's declaration of the bracket text as an opaque event does not add a real trigger; it is the same defect restated in the model's own terms, so it is not a competent rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: lane_change -> cruise must be triggered by the named 'lane change is completed' event, not merely guarded.

issues.expected: The collision avoidance system scope (CollisionAvoidanceSystem) must be entered from the overall model root so its declared initial edge [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive is a live default entry.
issues.observed: fcstm_model text declares only `[*] -> AutonomousMode;` at root scope; CollisionAvoidanceSystem has no root-owned entry edge. inspection_equivalent_facts marks CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active as reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts.non_proved lists reachability:state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:71 as refuted. The owner-local edge transition:line:74 ([*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive) exists but its owning scope itself has no path from the model root.
issues.reason: NL12 establishes that the collision avoidance system begins in collision_avoidance_deactive, i.e., an owner-scoped initial-entry obligation. The exact source/model comparison shows the owner-local edge exists (line 74) but is dead because the owning composite CollisionAvoidanceSystem has no entry edge from the top-level root ([*] -> AutonomousMode only). This is exactly the frontier's 'composite that owns required downstream behavior but lacks default entry' pattern, and initial_entry is the closest frozen property, though V1/S2 alone cannot capture the missing root-level composite entry, so predicate_id remains null for W1.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The owner-local initial edge collision_avoidance_deactive itself is correctly declared and would satisfy an owner-local contract if CollisionAvoidanceSystem were ever entered; the defect is upstream root reachability of the owning composite, not malformation of the edge itself, so this issue should not be read as invalidating the owner-local edge's own correctness.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem owner scope is never entered from root, so its owner-local initial edge to collision_avoidance_deactive is never exercised

issues.reason: Per frontier discipline every termination contract with state_role=termination_state must have its target ancestry and continuations audited even when the endpoint transition exists. Exact facts confirm FinishState has no outgoing edge and does not cycle back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode, so the termination obligation is satisfied; this candidate documents that audit outcome using the required predicate-null form since no frozen predicate directly certifies terminal stability, but is not asserting an unrebutted defect.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: This is actually the satisfied case: FinishState never re-enters or cycles, so the termination obligation itself is met; the LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic is deadlock-frontier evidence for a different property (deadlock_freedom on an operating state), not evidence against this termination contract. Because supplied deterministic facts here show a satisfied stable termination and not a defect, this row should be treated as informational rather than a genuine issue; retained only because a leaf-without-outgoing diagnostic exists at this exact locus and the frontier discipline requires auditing every termination contract's target ancestry explicitly.
issues.title: FinishState is a genuine terminal leaf with no outgoing continuation, satisfying stable termination for HighwayMode's completion obligation

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:74 (source [*], target collision_avoidance_deactive, scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem, reachable_from_initial=false); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for CollisionAvoidanceSystem and collision_avoidance_deactive; verify_facts.non_proved reachability refuted for state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:72.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem must initially enter collision_avoidance_deactive, and this initial entry must be operationally reachable so the required behavior can execute.
issues.observed: The owner-local initial edge '[*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive' (transition:line:74) exists and targets the correct state, but CollisionAvoidanceSystem itself has STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics and verify_facts reachability refuted, so this exact initial entry can never fire from the machine root.
issues.reason: Per the owner-scoping rule, this initial_entry contract's own typed obligation (owner=CollisionAvoidanceSystem/root of that scope, target=collision_avoidance_deactive) is structurally satisfied by transition:line:74. However, because the frontier discipline treats owner default entry and root reachability as independent properties and directs preserving both when each fails, and because the entry can never execute in practice, this candidate documents the operational non-effect of that structurally present edge as a predicate-null W1 concern tied to the exact initial_entry contract, rather than silently treating it as fully satisfied while its behavioral effect never occurs.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The owner-local initial edge itself is well-formed (correct owner, correct target), so under a strict reading limited only to owner-local edge correctness this contract's narrow obligation is satisfied; the unreachability is a distinct root-reachability defect captured separately in the derived reachability contract, and could be argued to fully absorb this concern, leaving the owner-local edge fact itself non-violative.
issues.title: Owner-local initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive exists but the owning composite is unreachable from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (line 71/72/73); verify_facts.non_proved reachability refuted for state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:71, state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:72, state:collision_avoidance_active:line:73; fcstm_model.text showing the sole root edge '[*] -> AutonomousMode'; canonical_source_ir.model.hierarchy_level=hierarchical with concurrent_regions.count=0.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance operating scope described by NL12/NL13 must be reachable from the top-level root so its activation/deactivation behavior can execute.
issues.observed: The root scope's only initial edge is '[*] -> AutonomousMode'; no transition anywhere in the closed FCSTM targets CollisionAvoidanceSystem from a reachable state, and inspection-equivalent diagnostics explicitly mark CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active as STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL; verify_facts independently refutes reachability for all three.
issues.reason: This is exactly the class of case the frontier discipline calls out: a required composite/operating scope absent from root reachability, independent of and not discharged by the owner-local initial-entry edge fact, and independent of any local endpoint existence inside the scope.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met...
issues.strongest_rebuttal: PlantUML syntactically declares CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a sibling top-level region under the same document, which could be read as implying it is a second concurrently-active root region; if that reading were adopted, the composite would be reachable by construction of a second top-level region rather than needing an explicit edge. However, the NL and canonical source model classify this diagram as sequential/hierarchical (hierarchy_level=hierarchical, concurrent_regions count=0), so no such implicit region semantics apply here.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite is unreachable from the machine root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for _pedestrian_detected_dist_to_rear_5_vel_30_dist_to_front_15_in_highway_dist_to_front_10_in_urban (reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer check_id 'event-consumer:_pedestrian_detected_...' status=refuted; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE referencing transition:line:75.
issues.expected: At least one consumer transition for the composite activation event must be reachable from the top-level root so the required activation behavior can actually occur.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers reports declared consumer_transition_refs=['transition:line:75'] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for this event; verify_facts.non_proved independently marks the corresponding event-consumer check as refuted; this is a direct consequence of CollisionAvoidanceSystem being unreachable from root.
issues.reason: Per frontier discipline, reachable event-consumer coverage is an independent property from owner entry and root reachability and must receive its own candidate even when the root cause is shared; declaration-only presence of the one consumer transition does not discharge the stronger reachable-consumer obligation implied by NL12's description of required activation behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The single declared consumer transition is structurally well-formed (correct source, target, and trigger binding) and the sole cause of unreachability is the enclosing composite's root disconnection, already captured by the derived reachability contract; one could argue this event-consumer fact adds no independent information beyond that root defect.
issues.title: Activation event for collision_avoidance_active has a declared but zero reachable consumer
